verdicts.reason: The account holds Rs 332,673.53 of traced victim funds (~44.7% of the disputed amount, exceeding the 25% threshold). Despite genuine indicators (16-year-old business account, no mule links), the lien only freezes the victim's money (4% of balance), and the 200-phone-sharing cluster warrants caution.

This layer-1 account received the full disputed amount directly from the victim and still holds 52.6% tainted funds, exceeding the 50% tainted-share threshold. The lien of Rs 330,788.47 is proportionate to the traced victim money remaining in the account, and the large device-sharing cluster (195 accounts) does not negate the trace.

This account's tainted share is only 4.75% (well below 50%) and it holds just 7.1% of the disputed amount (well below 25%), so it meets neither lien threshold. All signals—20-year-old business account, zero pass-through, no outflows, no shared identifiers—confirm a genuinely innocent absorbing account whose own funds should not be disturbed.
